declarations.what: Norris's General Directory of Chicago for 1844, the two parts of the volume that are PROSE AND TABLES rather than a list of names: the DESCRIPTION AND HISTORICAL SKETCH, printed pages 5-20 (leaves 15-30), and the STATISTICAL ACCOUNT, printed pages 66-78 (leaves 76-88). Read as dated town findings — every claim carries `town_finding: true` and a `describes_date` naming the year the STATEMENT describes, which for most of them is not 1844 and for four of them is 1835.

not_read_and_why.the 1843 census table on printed page 76: Norris prints his 1843 census as a wide ruled table and archive.org's OCR wove its columns into a single stream of bare numbers with the headings floated out of place. The three nativity ROWS survive as rows and are quoted; the counts beside them cannot be attached to a column from this text and are NOT asserted. What is asserted from that page is what survives unambiguously: 1,177 families, and the grand totals 4,853 (1840) and 7,580 (1843). Closing the rest needs the page image, and n1844_tf_062 is the standing declaration that it has not been closed.
not_read_and_why.the pairing of year to figure in the tra: Read off the ORDER in which the OCR set the two tables — exports first, then imports — because the ruling that separated them did not survive. Stated in n1844_tf_064 rather than left implicit.
